In C#, "int" stands for integer and is used to store whole numbers without decimals (e.g., 5, 10, 100).
If your value contains decimal points, you should use "double" (e.g., 3.14, 2.75), which can store floating-point numbers.
Choosing the correct data type helps your program run correctly and efficiently.
